_what: What makes a footage candidate a host show - a podcast, an interview, a talk show (late night, morning, daytime), a press junket, a roundtable, a reaction, a review or commentary video. Somebody else's host (or a press interviewer) talking to camera under our narration is not backdrop footage: a viewer wrote 'Stop stealing content. Especially from the basement yard podcast' under the Reel vanguards-doomsday, which ran 16 of 16 clips out of Zenith's own 'Countdown to Vanguards: Doomsday Official Podcast'. The user said yes to the rule on 2026-10-20. Trailers, official clips, featurettes and on-set footage stay as before.
_read_by: agents/trend-hunter/scripts/host_show.py (footage_candidates.select_candidates and footage_supplement.sieve); the footage indexer's pool-reuse sieve reads the same lists
_rule: A host show is refused as a footage candidate with reason_code 'host_show' - whatever its origin: `origin: official` does NOT exempt it (the Zenith podcast is on Zenith Entertainment, the Kimmel and Fallon interviews are on their own registered channels). One exception, read off existing fields only: the topic's subject is a person (title_ref.kind 'person' whose name is that person, or a supplement entity of kind 'person') and the source's title names that person - their own interview (Danny Vermette's on Pop Culture Confidential for a story about him). A second, mechanical one: the topic's own name names the show (a story about The Late Show is told with The Late Show). The kept candidate carries `host_show.exception`.
_lists: Two lists read on the upload's title and channel name (never the description - past its first lines it is boilerplate): `shows` (named programmes and the channels that are such a programme) and `formats` (the words that say what kind of upload it is). `natures` are the footage natures (footage_candidates.classify) that are a talk in themselves. `facets` are the search facets that alone, on an upload whose own metadata says nothing (nature 'unknown'), mark it. A show entry with `fields: ["channel_title"]` is read on the channel only, and with `whole: true` it must be the whole channel name, because its name is an ordinary phrase elsewhere ('The View', 'Today', 'Collider' - the Large Hadron one is in science titles). A `formats` entry with `official: false` is not read on an official channel: there 'review' and 'reaction' are promo words ('The Social Reckoning - Social Review', Example Pictures, NMkieXpknkg; 'Fan Reactions' spots). To extend: append an entry with `code`, `pattern` (a regex, matched case-insensitively on whole tokens) and either `seen_in` (a real upload out of a real batch) or `named_by` (who named it).
_natures_note: A nature is a signal only (1) off a channel that is not official - a studio's own 'Talk about hanging by a thread | RENNICK' (Prime Video, P1N23x_ozIU) or 'tea so hot, I gotta sit down' (Example+) is a promo the interview rule reads as a talk, and a studio's own recap is cut from the work's footage (ExampleStream 'Season 3 Recap' for the-diplomat, audit CF-0818: clean) - an official channel's podcast or talk show is caught by its words (`shows`, `formats`), never by its nature alone; and (2) when the nature was read off the title or the room (footage_candidates.classify_with_source `title` / `room`), not off the head of the description: the premiere arrivals of Delver (fczumiLXgUE, -va_sLlPyDk) read 'interview' off their descriptions and are event footage, not a host.
_spared: `spared_natures`: a show matched on the channel name only, with no other signal, on an upload whose nature is a cut of the work, is not a host show. For a programme (Fallon, Kimmel...) only a `trailer`; for a press outlet (`outlet: true` - they re-upload the work's own cuts beside their interviews) also a scene or episode clip and a promo: 'Paper Dragon | Official Trailer' on Showbiz Evening (5pHfzVnSERU) is the trailer, 'Taylor Sterling Surprises Dana Reyes During WNL Monologue' on Showbiz Evening is the monologue. Not a featurette: an outlet's 'behind the scenes' is its own correspondent's report. Trailers and official clips stay as before (the user, 2026-10-20).
